 Costa Rica’s Festival de la Luz Dec. 12: New Route, No Floats
 San Jose's Festival de la Luz runs Dec. 12 on a new route from Plaza de la Democracia to Paseo Colon, and without the usual floats this year.
 Home » News » Costa Rica’s Festival de la Luz Dec. 12: New Route, No Floats 
 Nov 14, 2026, 7:47 PM GMT-0400 • Nov 14, 2026, 7:47 PM GMT-0400 • 5 min read Share Share Email WhatsApp LinkedIn X Facebook 
 By Rolando Herrera 
 San José’s Festival de la Luz, Costa Rica’s big holiday parade, takes place on Saturday, December 12, 2026, on a new route and without the usual floats.
 Plan to watch along the new route, which runs from Plaza de la Democracia to Torre Mercedes on Paseo Colón, Teletica reported. Start time had not been announced.

 The festival will be held without floats after public institutions withdrew, San José mayor Diego Miranda said, according to La Nación .
 At a Glance 
 Date: Saturday, December 12.
 Route: Plaza de la Democracia to Torre Mercedes, Paseo Colón.
 Floats: None this year.
 Start time: Not yet announced.
 City: San José, Costa Rica.
 The New Route 
 The parade starts at Plaza de la Democracia and ends at Torre Mercedes on Paseo Colón, councillors Juan Diego Gómez and Marco Tulio Ramírez confirmed to Telenoticias.
 It is the third route in three years. In 2025 the festival ran a closed circuit around Parque Metropolitano La Sabana, Teletica said.
 El Observador reported that the parade returns to Paseo Colón and Avenida Segunda, its traditional streets, and that some logistics were still unconfirmed.
 No Floats This Year 
 Miranda said six public institutions withdrew their participation, and the float format depended on their funding, La Nación reported.
 He linked the withdrawals to politics. Banco Popular said its decision followed marketing and institutional strategy criteria, La Nación said.
 CRHoy also reported that the parade will have no floats after several entities decided not to take part.
 Bands 
 Fourteen bands will march this year, up from 10 last year, according to Mayor Miranda, El Observador reported.
 Banda Cedes Don Bosco, last year’s winner, ranked first in auditions. It is also set to march in the 2027 Rose Parade in Pasadena, El Observador said.
 Bands from Orotina, Acosta, La Fortuna, Zarcero, Puriscal and Alajuela are among those taking part, with the Banda Municipal de San José as host.
 Bands are judged on visual effect, musical effect, overall effect, color guard and dance.
 The city was also evaluating large balloons, similar to those in US parades, El Observador said.
 What to Expect 
 The festival is traditionally known for marching bands and lit floats. This year the city is seeking a new format, with private companies expected to take part, La Nación said.
 Check the Municipalidad de San José’s announcements closer to the date for the program, start time and road closures.
 Viewing Spots 
 Paseo Colón, a wide avenue west of downtown, is expected to be the main viewing area. Arrive early for a spot along the sidewalk.
 Crowds are large, so agree on a meeting point and keep valuables secure.
 Bring water and a light layer, since you may wait outside for a couple of hours.
 Getting Around 
 Roads near the route will close on parade day. Plan to walk or use buses and taxis, and expect heavy traffic in central San José in the afternoon and evening.
 Details Still Pending 
 The route, format and funding have all changed in recent months, so treat this year’s plan as subject to change until the city publishes its final program.
 Look for the start time, road closures and viewing zones in the municipality’s announcements in early December.
 Weather 
 December is the start of the dry season in the Central Valley, and evenings in San José are mild. A light jacket is usually enough.
 Travel to Costa Rica 
 Juan Santamaría International Airport near San José is served by many nonstop flights from the United States, and December fares rise quickly.
 Some lounges at the airport have been closed, as Deep Arrival reported on San José airport lounge closures .
 Health Notes 
 Costa Rica has reported a rise in dengue cases this year, as covered in our report on dengue in Costa Rica . Use insect repellent, especially at dusk.
 Where to Stay 
 Hotels near Paseo Colón, La Sabana and central San José put you within walking distance of the route.
 Many visitors pass through San José on the way to the coast or the volcanoes.
 The festival can fit neatly into a first or last night in the capital.
 Visiting With Kids 
 The parade is a family event. Bring water and snacks, and choose a spot away from the densest crowds near the start.
